_note: Companion fault rules for scenarios/bad_payload_fault.json. POST each item to /admin/v1/faults after the run is generated. Kept separate from the scenario on purpose: declaring a fault must never change the generated dataset or its canonical digest (ADR-006, INV-12).

rules._expect: Request 3 returns 200 with one fewer deal. The downstream connector must detect the gap; the canonical digest must not change.
One deal_id appears twice in a page. Downstream idempotency must absorb it.
Schema validation downstream must reject the item rather than store a partial record.
A finite but absurd decimal. Downstream must refuse it without exhausting memory (WF-067).
A retryable transport-shaped failure with a concrete backoff hint.
snapshot_seq goes backwards. A consumer tracking it must notice rather than advance its watermark.

_not_covered_here: TCP reset, half-open connections, DNS failure and MTU changes need a network proxy; a middleware cannot produce them, and a rule that claimed to would make a test that proves nothing (section 6.4).
Disk full, read-only mounts and SIGKILL are storage/process faults driven by the failpoints in simulator.persistence.failpoints and the chaos suite, not by this API.
Power-loss durability is NOT TESTED. kill -9 is not a power cut (WF-087).
